title: Snapp v. James River Presbytery
disposition_detail: Sole issue answered 'No'; complaint denied. The SJC upheld James River Presbytery's October 1997 action sustaining TE Andrew Conrad's examination. Vote: 15 concurring, 6 dissenting, 1 recused, 2 absent. No remand or other relief.
first_summary: The SJC denied Byron Snapp's complaint against James River Presbytery, which had sustained an ordination examination despite the candidate's anthropomorphic view of the Genesis creation days. Because no General Assembly had declared that view out of accord with the Westminster Standards and a study committee was examining creation views, the SJC declined to decide the creation-day question and upheld the Presbytery's authority. A six-member dissent urged an exception or study committee.
summary: The complaint challenged James River Presbytery's approval of an ordination examination in which the candidate called the Genesis creation days God's anthropomorphic work days, not necessarily twenty-four-hour days. The complainant argued that view conflicted with WCF I.9. The SJC denied the complaint and answered 'No' to whether the Presbytery erred; the examination stood. It held the Presbytery had authority and discretion, no General Assembly had declared anthropomorphic days contrary to the Standards, and an advisory-committee study left the SJC unwilling to decide creation-day length. A six-member dissent sought an exception and study-committee referral.
